source_policy.attribution: The Way to Yahuweh; identify the individual document and its cited underlying edition or manuscript source.
source_policy.handling: Use as an additional transcription or comparison source, not as an automatic substitute for institutional manuscript images or critical editions.
required_metadata: underlying edition and page/plate references where supplied
limitations: The downloadable documents are editorial transcriptions or research documents, not photographic facsimiles.
A file's manuscript label does not by itself establish that every displayed reading is independently verified against the original manuscript.
Separate manuscript witnesses and comparison texts must remain distinguished.
The site owner's editorial interpretations must not be presented as institutional consensus or as the manuscript's unmediated wording.
This is a collection of downloadable documents, not one unified critical edition or manuscript catalogue; each file must be assessed and attributed separately.
A provider's transcription or PDF text layer may contain transcription, OCR, spacing, or extraction errors; verify readings against the rendered document and the cited scholarly edition.
A PDF heading or displayed line break is not automatically a manuscript fragment, column, or line coordinate.
Only files whose individual source, scope, and CC BY-SA 4.0 terms have been checked may be imported; do not infer that every file on the site has identical content or coverage.
Do not merge these transcriptions with Qumran-Digital, ETCBC, or published DJD readings; preserve each source as a distinct witness or edition.

handling.square_brackets: Retain exactly. The Wikisource edition uses square brackets to identify Hebrew text supplied where the Hebrew manuscript original is absent; these are editorial Hebrew retroversions, not manuscript readings.
handling.unbracketed_text: Treat as Kahana's Hebrew edition based on manuscript evidence, not as a diplomatic transcription of a single codex. Link to a specific Genizah, Qumran, or Masada witness only after passage-level verification.
handling.incomplete_pages: The Wikisource work page states that transcription is in progress and does not represent the work in full. Missing online text must not be mistaken for an ancient manuscript lacuna.
handling.comparison: Compare same-passage readings with Greek and Syriac witnesses independently. Never silently merge versions or translate Greek/Syriac words into Hebrew and label them as preserved Hebrew.

limitations: The edition is a printed scholarly compilation, not an original ancient manuscript.
Kahana reports that some Hebrew portions absent from the manuscripts were supplied as Hebrew translations from Greek and Syriac by Kamenetsky.
The Wikisource transcription is explicitly incomplete; it is not a complete machine-readable text.
No manuscript shelfmark, fragment, column, or line coordinate is inferred from Kahana's printed text alone.

Kahana's own 1912 preface explicitly states that the first two chapters and some verses of chapter 3 were not preserved in Hebrew manuscripts and were translated into Hebrew from Greek and Syriac by Dr. Kamenetzky.
The printed Hebrew in those passages is editorial retroversion, not an ancient Hebrew manuscript witness; square brackets and the chapter-level source note must remain visible.
